docs.purpose: The operator's window on push notifications. It lists what was sent, to whom, when and of what type, with device identifiers partly hidden, and lets the operator fire a real test notification to a chosen device and see the delivery receipt. It also shows, read-only, whether notifications are currently switched off or throttled, linking to the control panel for the one place those settings can actually be changed.
docs.data_story: It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through 2 contracts: `/api/admin/notifications`, `/api/admin/notifications/test-send`. Behind those contracts, the data comes from `device_tokens`, `logic_variables`, `notification_dispatches`, `notifications` and `user_profiles`.
docs.under_126: **RE-PROJECT** — it writes nothing and holds no Layer-3 store, so the move is short — the server already assembles the payload and only the rendering is client-side. It renders through the LIST renderer (a collection with declared pagination, recycling and empty/offline states), reading by reference: `/api/admin/notifications`, `/api/admin/notifications/test-send`. Its `owns.components[]` declares `src/components/admin/NotificationsTool.tsx`.

versioning.why: Both contracts are called only from this tool and the user-detail card; nothing outside the repo consumes them, so a shape change is one commit.

inputs.why: The dispatch log, the device tokens, the user preferences and the three kill-switch values all arrive through GET /api/admin/notifications.

outputs.why: Test-send posts and waits; it deliberately writes NO notification_dispatches or notifications row, so the log it sits beside stays a record of real dispatches only.
outputs.rollback: None is possible — the side effect is a push already delivered to a device. The only guard is that the route refuses any credential other than a real session.

state.why: It runs under the root PersistQueryClientProvider with no store of its own; the page itself is force-dynamic so the shell is never statically cached.

staleness.why: The page declares dynamic = force-dynamic and the route sets no cache directive, so the dispatch log is read on every request.

session.why: There is no admin Postgres role: classifyRoute sends every /admin/* path down the admin arm, and the real boundary is verifyAdminAuth reading profiles.is_admin on the route. Both contracts call it on their first line, and test-send additionally requires authMethod === "session", so neither a CI token nor a break-glass key can fire a push.

rls_class.why: notification_dispatches, notifications, device_tokens and user_profiles are four of the ten Class-A auth.uid()-owned tables; the admin reads them through the service role, which is the only principal a Class-A policy lets past for another user's rows.

checks.why: Every push token leaves the route masked, on both the dispatch rows and the device list — an unmasked token in an admin payload is a credential leak, so this is a pre-render gate.
The kill-switch and throttle values render read-only and deep-link to the Control Panel, so logic_variables keeps exactly one write path rather than two.
A day with no dispatches must render the declared empty state, not a blank table that reads as a broken page.

errors.why: Every failure path on both contracts returns the { data, error, meta } envelope with a code, and the tool renders from it.

classes.ui: envelope error — a non-session credential cannot test-send
envelope error rendered in the panel

emits.why: Read telemetry is deliberately omitted (the log renders no PII), but the test-send route emits admin_action_performed to PostHog with a hashed admin uid. That is the only trace a real push leaves.

offers.why: An internal operator tool renders no sponsored placement; no offers/placements table is reached from any file it owns.

metering.why: Nothing here is billable or quota-bearing: no usage_events / ledger write is reached from this surface or its contracts.

config.why: It renders three tunables read-only as the dispatch kill-switch status panel; the write path for all three is the Spec 86 Control Panel, not this page.

logic_variables.name: notifications_dispatch_enabled
logic_variables.why: Rendered as status only; an absent row shows the seeded default rather than failing the page.

sharing.why: /api/admin/notifications is also read by NotificationsCard, which renders inside the user-detail page.

limitations.what: POST /api/admin/notifications/test-send delivers a real push with no admin_audit_log row
limitations.measured: The route emits a PostHog track() only; it does not import src/lib/admin/admin-audit.ts, so an operator-triggered push to a real user's device leaves no audit row.
limitations.check_id: none — no checks[] kind covers "an admin mutation writes an admin_audit_log row"; escalated per Spec 128 §4

limitations.what: The response carries a fourth top-level key outside the envelope
touch_target_min_px has no legal answer for a desktop-only admin page
limitations.measured: The schema allows only UNRESEARCHED or an integer >= 44, and nothing in this surface declares a 44px floor (grep for min-h-[44 / h-11 over its owned files returns nothing).
limitations.check_id: none — vocabulary gap, escalated per Spec 128 §4

notes: Archetype LIST for the dispatch log, which is the page's spine; it also embeds a small test-send FORM and a read-only status panel. Deliberately read-only on the kill-switch/throttle values so there is one write path for logic_variables (the Spec 86 Control Panel), not two. The page sets `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`. identity.owner is UNRESEARCHED estate-wide: no owner registry exists in the tree, so naming one would be an invention rather than a measurement. a11y.touch_target_min_px is UNRESEARCHED because its vocabulary (UNRESEARCHED or an integer >= 44) has no member for a desktop-only admin page that declares no floor. AUDIT FINDING: POST /api/admin/notifications/test-send delivers a real push to a real device with no admin_audit_log row - only a PostHog track().

measured_gate.why: classifyRoute('/admin/notifications') matches the admin-pages arm via `pathname.startsWith('/admin/')` -> 'admin'.

programme.why: Notifications: one device-token registry and one preference set across both products.
